# Load libraries


```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "plotly", "kableExtra", "knitr", "maps"))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, lubridate
library(plotly)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(maps)        # provides map_data("world")
```

# Import dataset & display the first few rows

The data file lives in the `data/` folder of this project.

```{r}
sars <- read.csv("~/Downloads/sars_2003_complete_dataset_clean.csv.xls",
                 header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(sars) <- c("Date", "Country", "Confirmed Cases",
                    "Patient Deaths", "Patients Recovered")

head(sars)
```

```{r}
# Dimension of dataset
dim(sars)
```

```{r}
# Columns and class
sapply(sars, class)
```

```{r}
# Duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(sars))
```

```{r}
# Convert date from character to Date
sars$Date <- as.Date(sars$Date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
sum(is.na(sars$Date))   # should be 0; if not, the date format doesn't match
```

```{r}
sars %>% arrange(desc(Date)) %>% head()
```

```{r}
length(unique(sars$Date))

sarsconfirm <- sars %>% group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(confirmed_case = sum(`Confirmed Cases`)) %>% as.data.frame()
sarsdeath <- sars %>% group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(death_case = sum(`Patient Deaths`)) %>% as.data.frame()
sarsrecover <- sars %>% group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(recovered_case = sum(`Patients Recovered`)) %>% as.data.frame()

head(sarsconfirm)
head(sarsdeath)
head(sarsrecover)
```

```{r}
# Combine data from above and reshape from wide to long
sarscases <- sarsconfirm %>%
  left_join(sarsdeath, by = "Date") %>%
  left_join(sarsrecover, by = "Date") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(confirmed_case, death_case, recovered_case),
               names_to = "casetype", values_to = "count")
head(sarscases)
```

```{r}
# Confirmed cases, patient deaths and patients recovered over time
# (the counts in the data are cumulative totals)
ggplot(sarscases, aes(x = Date, y = count, color = casetype)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Cumulative Cases by Case Type") +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("Number of cases")
```

```{r}
# Top ten countries by recovery rate
# Counts are cumulative, so use each country's final (maximum) values.
recovery_rate <- sars %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarize(RecoveryRate = 100 * max(`Patients Recovered`) / max(`Confirmed Cases`))

top_ones <- recovery_rate %>% arrange(desc(RecoveryRate))
most_recovered <- head(top_ones, 10)
most_recovered

ggplot(most_recovered, aes(x = reorder(Country, -RecoveryRate), y = RecoveryRate, fill = Country)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "Country", y = "Recovery Rate (%)", title = "Top Ten Countries Recovery Rate") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
summary(recovery_rate$RecoveryRate)
```

```{r}
# Boxplot of recovery rate for all countries
ggplot(data = recovery_rate, aes(x = "All countries", y = RecoveryRate)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "yellow1") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  ggtitle("Recovery rate of all countries")
```

```{r}
# Table of country names with their recovery rates
kable(recovery_rate) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = FALSE,
                position = "left", fixed_thead = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, border_right = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "red")
```

```{r}
# Top ten countries by death count
country_totals <- sars %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarize(totConfirmed = max(`Confirmed Cases`),
            totDeaths    = max(`Patient Deaths`),
            totRecovered = max(`Patients Recovered`))

top_country <- country_totals %>% arrange(desc(totDeaths)) %>% head(10)
top_country

ggplot(top_country, aes(x = reorder(Country, -totDeaths), y = totDeaths, fill = Country)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "Country", y = "Death Count", title = "Top Ten Countries Death Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
# Total number of confirmed cases by country
sars %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarise(maxx = max(`Confirmed Cases`)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Country, maxx), y = maxx)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "red") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14)) +
  labs(x = "Countries", y = "Confirmed cases",
       title = "Total number of cases by Country")
```

```{r}
# Data frame with maximum confirmed cases per country
value_data <- sars %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), maxCases = max(`Confirmed Cases`))

# Rename countries so they match the names used by map_data("world").
# Add more pairs here if the check below shows unmatched names.
country_fix <- c("United States" = "USA",
                 "United Kingdom" = "UK")
value_data$Country <- dplyr::recode(value_data$Country, !!!country_fix)

# Countries in the data that will NOT appear on the map (names don't match)
setdiff(value_data$Country, unique(map_data("world")$region))

kable(t(value_data %>%
          select(Country, maxCases) %>%
          arrange(desc(maxCases))))
```

```{r}
# Map of the most confirmed cases worldwide
worldmap <- map_data("world")
merged_data <- merge(x = worldmap, y = value_data,
                     by.x = "region", by.y = "Country", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(order)

map_plot <- ggplot(data = merged_data,
                   aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = maxCases)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", na.value = "grey90") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(fill = "Maximum Cases", title = "Maximum confirmed SARS cases by country")

ggplotly(map_plot)
```
